scope: Core Hermes assembly, security response headers, and tooling follow-up
worktree: uncommitted implementation over the earlier cleanup pass

hermes.before: original production code with the added assembly benchmark

paired.order: before/after on even samples, after/before on odd samples; each sample starts a fresh process
paired.baseline_build: go test -overlay=<overlay.json> -c; overlay restores HEAD versions of hermes/{apply,columnar,columnar_pushdown,indexes,store}.go and security/middleware.go. Hide new columnar_candidates.go and columnar_candidates_test.go. Keep the assembly benchmark.
paired.after_build: go test -c with the final working tree

initial_comparisons.writes: The initial 200ms series suggested a 6–7% batch/rebuild slowdown. Its baseline preceded order tracking but followed pointer lookup extraction. The full-HEAD alternating comparison supersedes that timing claim.
initial_comparisons.http: The initial 200ms series suggested a 3% secured-chain slowdown. The alternating comparison supersedes that timing claim. Raw files remain available.

limits: No hardware performance counters or retained RSS capture.
Allocation bytes describe temporary work, not total resident memory.
Write benchmarks have amortized growth and are not allocation gates.
No service-backed, consumer application, or production latency claim.

audience_digest.change: Length-prefixed audience identifiers replace delimiter framing.
audience_digest.public_contract: No wire, persistence, or API change; internal process-local cache keys change.

unordered.fixture: 128 or 10000 rows, followed by one decreasing-timestamp patch. Limit 50.
unordered.result: Heap retention is O(K); existing delta-index reconciliation can allocate O(N) keys. This is not the ordered fast-path workload.
